title: GPU autoscaler bridge Terraform module: safe upgrades, dual-mode ASG/Karpenter integration
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal: Build a single, well-documented Terraform module that provisions GPU node groups in Private (VPC) environments and provides a safe integration layer with both ASG-based and Karpenter-based autoscalers. The module should encapsulate: nodegroup lifecycle resources, node upgrade/cordon/drain helpers, healthcheck hooks, capacity fallback policies, and a policy-driven selector that allows runtime switching (or blue/green rollout) between ASG and Karpenter for the same workload.

Why this ticket: customers deploying Redwood Private require predictable GPU capacity and low-risk upgrades. Existing modules are split between ASG and Karpenter variants; operations teams have no standardized guardrails for rolling driver/kernel upgrades or degraded autoscaler failover. This module reduces toil and centralizes best practices (taints, labels, lifecycle hooks, node termination handlers, and health probes).
technical_approach:
1) Design an opinionated terraform module with input flags: mode = {asg|karpenter|hybrid}, gpu_type, min/max/desired, upgrade_strategy = {drain-first|cordon-drain-batch}, health_probe_endpoint, termination_grace_seconds.
2) Provide optional launch template and user-data snippets that register node metadata for runtime routing and observability.
3) Implement AWS lifecycle hooks (for ASG) and Karpenter provisioner TTL/constraints for Karpenter variant; expose a lightweight migration plan that can perform blue/green nodegroup switchover.
4) Add a set of healthcheck resources and a small Lambda/controller glue to mark unhealthy nodes so autoscalers can respect pool health.
5) Enable automated canary upgrades with a default of 2 nodes at a time and automatic rollback if node health falls below threshold.
6) Emit clear outputs: instance_profile, subnet_ids, nodepool_tags, drift_detection_metric_name for monitoring.

Trade-offs considered: keep module opinionated to reduce config surface vs allowing full customization. We choose opinionated defaults but expose escape-hatches for advanced customers (hooks, extra_user_data).
acceptance_criteria: Module can create GPU node pool in a Private VPC and attach either ASG or Karpenter provisioning depending on mode flag
Support rolling upgrades: cordon+drain policy with configurable batch size and automatic rollback on health regression
Automated healthchecks (kube-probe + cloud metric) trigger fallback policy: scale up alternative pool or route traffic away
Documentation and example usage for hybrid migration (ASG -> Karpenter) that completes without >2x expected cost spike
Integration tests: terraform apply/destroy in ephemeral account, upgrade simulation, and canary failure rollback validated
Observability: module emits metrics and tags compatible with Redwood Console dashboards (tokenized nodepool tag)
Security review signoff on user-data scripts and IAM roles
plan:
Week 1: module skeleton, inputs/outputs, basic ASG flow + docs.
Week 2: Karpenter provisioner variant, hybrid selector, and lifecycle hooks.
Week 3: cordon/drain tooling, healthcheck lambda/controller, E2E tests.
Week 4: documentation, examples, security review, and partner testing with Solutions Eng.

Deliverables: terraform module, example root module for private-vpc, upgrade runbook, automated test suite (CI), and a short confluence design doc.
testing_plan:
- Unit: terraform validate and tflint for module.
- Integration: CI job that spins up ephemeral VPC in sandbox account using minimal GPU quota, run canary upgrade (simulate kernel/driver update) and assert no more than configured batch size replaced.
- Failure injection: terminate nodes during canary and ensure rollback path triggers and alternative pool scales as configured.
- Performance: measure cold-start time for Karpenter vs ASG scaled nodes and record in test report.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge module behind feature flag in private deployments.
2) Enable for internal staging namespace and run synthetic workloads for 48h.
3) Offer to 2 pilot customers with solutions engineering support.
4) Gradual ramp to all Private clusters over 4 weeks with monitoring and SLA guardrails.

Rollback: revert terraform to previous module version and trigger cordon+drain to move workloads back to previous pool.
